case.question: Which two operational benefits led to selecting the Moon's south polar region for Artemis III?
case.gold_answer: The south polar region offers access to persistently illuminated areas and potential access to surface-accessible volatile deposits.

retrieved.title: Retrieved 1: artemis_south_pole_benefits | South polar operational benefits
retrieved.text: The Moon's south polar region was selected because it offers two clear operational benefits: access to persistently illuminated areas and potential access to surface-accessible volatile deposits.

retrieved.title: Retrieved 2: artemis_science_objectives | Seven Artemis III science objectives
retrieved.text: The seven overarching Artemis III science objectives are understanding planetary processes, understanding the character and origin of lunar polar volatiles, interpreting the impact history of the Earth-Moon system, revealing the record of the ancient sun and astronomical environment, observing the universe and local space environment from a unique location, conducting experimental science in the lunar environment, and investigating and mitigating exploration risks.

retrieved.title: Retrieved 3: artemis_south_pole_definition | South polar region definition
retrieved.text: The report defines the Moon's south polar region as the area within 6 degrees of latitude from the lunar south pole.
